name: A year of books of a Hong Kong trading and consulting company that files no periodic return

documents.why: A domestic sale of services, HK-S-NA: the not-subject code posts the line's base and nothing else — no tax line, no declaration box.
A domestic sale of goods, HK-S-NA on the goods side too: the code draws no distinction the way a real turnover tax would between what is sold.

An export of goods to a customer outside Hong Kong: HK-S-NA applies exactly as it does to V2's domestic sale, because a territorial system with no turnover tax at all draws no export/domestic line to begin with.
A credit note against V2, a partial return of goods — the golden's sale-side credit note.
A second domestic service sale, to spread the scenario across more than one month and leave an invoice a part-payment settles only partly.
A third domestic goods sale, settled by nothing in this scenario — an open receivable the trial balance has to carry at the year end.
A domestic purchase of trading inventory, HK-P-NA: the purchase side of the not-subject code, posting the base and nothing to recover.
A recurring domestic expense, office rent, paid in full by E3 — the golden's matched payment on the purchase side.

An import of raw materials from a supplier outside Hong Kong: no import tax posts, because Hong Kong is a free port that charges no general tax on goods crossing its border, and HK-P-NA reads the same on an import as on a domestic purchase.
A credit note against P1, a partial return of defective stock — the golden's purchase-side credit note, beside CN1 on the sale side.

A purchase of a fixed asset, computer equipment, booked straight to the balance sheet rather than to an expense account — proof HK-P-NA posts its base wherever the document line's own account sends it, and nowhere of its own choosing.
A recurring administrative purchase, the fee for running the Mandatory Provident Fund scheme every Hong Kong employer has to operate for its staff.

A recurring administrative purchase, accounting and company secretarial fees — the annual return every Hong Kong private company delivers to the Companies Registry within 42 days of its incorporation anniversary depends on one.

payments.why: An inbound payment that exactly settles V1 — the golden's matched payment on the sale side.
An inbound part-payment on account, matched to nothing — the golden's unmatched payment and the open item a return computed from matchings has to survive.
An outbound payment that exactly settles P2 — the matched payment on the purchase side.
An outbound part-payment on account to a supplier, matched to nothing — the unmatched payment on the purchase side.
